subject: reasoning
question: Statements: All cats are animals. All animals are mammals. Conclusion: All cats are mammals.

explanation.simple: All A are B, and All B are C -> All A are C is valid.
steps: Cats subset of Animals subset of Mammals.

methods.name: Venn Diagram
steps: Concentric circles: Cats inside Animals inside Mammals.

explanation.exam_tip: Transitivity of 'All': All A are B + All B are C => All A are C.

subject: reasoning
question: Statements: Some mangoes are apples. Some apples are bananas. Conclusions: I. Some mangoes are bananas. II. Some apples are mangoes.

explanation.simple: Some mangoes are apples directly converts to Some apples are mangoes (II follows). Mangoes and bananas may not overlap (I does not follow).
steps: Conversion of 'Some A are B' is 'Some B are A'.
No definite relation between Mango and Banana.

methods.name: Immediate Inference
steps: Some A are B => Some B are A.

explanation.exam_tip: 'Some A are B' can always be reversed to 'Some B are A'.

subject: reasoning
question: Statements: No dog is a cat. All cats are pets. Conclusion: Some pets are not dogs.

explanation.simple: Cats are pets, and no cat is a dog. The pets that are cats can never be dogs. Hence some pets are definitely not dogs.

methods.name: Deduction
steps: Some pets (the cats) are not dogs.

explanation.exam_tip: 'All B are C' + 'No A is B' implies 'Some C are not A'.

subject: reasoning
question: Statements: All pens are pencils. No pencil is an eraser. Conclusion: No pen is an eraser.

explanation.simple: All pens are inside pencils, and pencils have zero overlap with erasers. Pens can never touch erasers.

methods.name: Universal Negative
steps: All A are B + No B is C => No A is C.

explanation.exam_tip: If outer circle has no relation, inner circle also has no relation.

subject: reasoning
question: Statements: Some books are papers. All papers are files. Conclusions: I. Some books are files. II. All files are papers.

explanation.simple: Some books are papers + All papers are files -> Some books are files (I follows). 'All papers are files' does NOT mean 'All files are papers' (II fails).
steps: II is a fallacy of illicit conversion.
explanation.exam_tip: 'All A are B' only converts to 'Some B are A'.

subject: reasoning
question: Statements: All cars are trains. Some trains are buses. Conclusions: I. Some cars are buses. II. Some buses are trains.

explanation.simple: Some trains are buses directly implies Some buses are trains (II follows). Cars and buses need not intersect (I does not follow).
steps: Cars and buses may have no overlap.
II is immediate conversion of statement 2.

methods.name: Venn Diagram
steps: Buses circle can touch trains without touching cars.

explanation.exam_tip: Do not assume intersection unless forced by statements.

subject: reasoning
question: Statements: No river is sea. No sea is ocean. Conclusions: I. Some rivers are oceans. II. No river is ocean.

explanation.simple: Two negative premises yield no definite conclusion. However, Conclusion I ('Some rivers are oceans') and II ('No river is ocean') form a complementary pair (I and E type). Thus, either I or II must follow.
steps: No definite link between River and Ocean.
I (Some) and E (No) form complementary pair.

methods.name: Complementary Pair Rule
steps: Subject and predicate same, one positive one negative -> Either/Or.

explanation.exam_tip: 'Some A are B' and 'No A is B' always make an Either-Or pair.

subject: reasoning
question: Statements: All stars are moons. All moons are planets. Conclusions: I. Some planets are stars. II. All stars are planets.

explanation.simple: All stars are planets (II follows). If all stars are planets, some planets must be stars (I follows). Both follow.

methods.name: Universal Syllogism
steps: All A are C, and Some C are A.

explanation.exam_tip: All implies Some.

subject: reasoning
question: Statements: Only a few doctors are lawyers. All lawyers are professionals. Conclusions: I. Some doctors are not lawyers. II. All doctors can be lawyers.

explanation.simple: 'Only a few A are B' means: Some A are B AND Some A are NOT B. Thus, I follows definitely. And because some doctors are NOT lawyers, all doctors CANNOT be lawyers (II is false).

methods.name: Modern Banking Concept
steps: Only a few A are B restricts 'All A are B'.

explanation.exam_tip: 'Only a few' prohibits 'All A being B'.

subject: reasoning
question: Statements: All flowers are red. No red is rose. Conclusions: I. No flower is rose. II. Some red are flowers.

explanation.simple: Flowers are inside Red, which has no intersection with Rose, so No flower is rose (I follows). And All flowers are red implies Some red are flowers (II follows). Both follow.
steps: I is true by negative universal.
explanation.exam_tip: Both universal negative and subaltern conversions hold.

subject: reasoning
question: Statements: Some birds are animals. No animal is reptile. All reptiles are insects. Conclusions: I. Some birds are not reptiles. II. No bird is reptile.

explanation.simple: The birds that are animals can never be reptiles. Hence, 'Some birds are not reptiles' definitely follows. But remaining birds could be reptiles, so 'No bird is reptile' is not certain.
steps: Some birds are not reptiles is certain.

methods.name: Definite Partial Negative
steps: Some A are B + No B is C => Some A are not C.

explanation.exam_tip: Look at the intersection of A and B.

subject: reasoning
question: Statements: All tables are chairs. Some chairs are sofas. All sofas are beds. Conclusions: I. Some tables are beds. II. Some beds are chairs.

explanation.simple: Some chairs are sofas, and all sofas are beds -> Some chairs are beds, which means Some beds are chairs (II follows). Tables and beds have no guaranteed connection (I does not follow).
steps: Sofas inside Beds, Sofas touch Chairs -> Beds touch Chairs.
explanation.exam_tip: Follow the link from Beds to Chairs through Sofas.

subject: reasoning
question: Statements: All rings are circles. Some circles are squares. No square is triangle. Conclusions: I. All rings being triangles is a possibility. II. Some circles are not triangles.

explanation.simple: Circles that are squares cannot be triangles, so 'Some circles are not triangles' is definitely true (II follows). Rings have no negative condition with triangles, so all rings being triangles is possible (I follows). Both follow.
steps: Squares that are circles cannot be triangles -> II true.
Rings can be completely inside triangles -> I true.
explanation.exam_tip: If there is no direct negative link, possibility is generally true.

subject: reasoning
question: Statements: Only laptops are computers. Some laptops are tablets. Conclusion: No computer is a tablet.

explanation.simple: 'Only A are B' means 'All B are A' and B CANNOT have overlap with any other element except A. Hence Computer cannot be tablet. 'No computer is a tablet' definitely follows.
steps: 'Only A are B' restricts B exclusively to A.
explanation.exam_tip: In 'Only A are B', B can never touch any third entity.

subject: reasoning
question: Statements: Some water is milk. No milk is tea. All tea is coffee. Conclusions: I. Some water is not tea. II. All coffee being milk is a possibility.

explanation.simple: Water that is milk cannot be tea -> 'Some water is not tea' definitely follows (I). Since all tea is coffee and no milk is tea, if all coffee were milk, tea would also be milk (contradiction). So II is false.

methods.name: Possibility Test
steps: Tea cannot be milk -> Coffee containing Tea cannot be fully inside milk.

explanation.exam_tip: If a subset cannot touch B, the superset cannot be entirely inside B.

subject: reasoning
question: Statements: Many fruits are sweet. Most sweet are sour. Conclusions: I. Some fruits are sour. II. No fruit is sour.

explanation.simple: 'Many' and 'Most' represent 'Some'. Two 'Some' statements give no definite conclusion between Fruits and Sour. But 'Some fruits are sour' and 'No fruit is sour' form a complementary pair (I/E). Hence Either I or II follows.
explanation.exam_tip: 'Many', 'most', 'almost all' are treated as 'Some' in syllogisms.

subject: reasoning
question: Statements: All metals are hard. No hard is soft. Some soft are ductile. Conclusions: I. Some metals are ductile is a possibility. II. Some ductile are not hard. III. No metal is soft.

options.text: All I, II, and III follow

explanation.simple: III: Metals inside Hard, Hard disjoint with Soft -> No metal is soft (true). II: Ductile that are Soft cannot be Hard -> Some ductile are not hard (true). I: Metals can overlap with Ductile outside Soft -> Possibility is true. All three follow.
steps: I, II, and III are all logically valid.
explanation.exam_tip: Evaluate each conclusion independently in multi-conclusion questions.

subject: reasoning
question: Statements: Only a few lions are tigers. No tiger is leopard. All leopards are cheetahs. Conclusions: I. All lions can never be leopards. II. Some cheetahs are not tigers.

explanation.simple: Lions that are tigers can never be leopards, so all lions can never be leopards (I follows). Leopards that are cheetahs can never be tigers, so some cheetahs are not tigers (II follows). Both follow.
steps: I and II are both valid deductions.
explanation.exam_tip: 'Can never be' means definite negative relation.

subject: reasoning
question: Statements: 0% gold is silver. 100% silver is copper. Some copper is platinum. Conclusions: I. Some copper is not gold. II. All platinum being gold is a possibility.

explanation.simple: 0% = No, 100% = All. Copper that is silver cannot be gold -> Some copper is not gold (I follows). Platinum has no negative relation with gold -> Possibility holds (II follows). Both follow.
explanation.exam_tip: 0% means 'No', 100% means 'All', 1% to 99% means 'Some'.

subject: reasoning
question: Statements: Each sun is star. Every star is galaxy. Not a single galaxy is planet. Conclusions: I. No sun is planet. II. At least some galaxies are suns.

explanation.simple: 'Each' = All, 'Every' = All, 'Not a single' = No. Suns are inside Galaxies, and no galaxy is planet -> No sun is planet (I). Since all suns are galaxies, some galaxies are suns (II). Both follow.
explanation.exam_tip: 'Each' and 'Every' mean 'All'; 'Not a single' means 'No'.
